newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Australia to fund demining in Cambodia, Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: Australia to fund demining in Cambodia, Mozambique.

text.p: Australia called on Thursday for a global ban on landmines -- the "great scourge of our day" -- and announced it was contributing new funds for mine-clearance in Cambodia and Mozambique.
In a speech, Foreign Minister Alexander Downer also urged the Disarmament Conference to start negotiations to halt production of plutonium and highly-enriched uranium used in making nuclear weapons.

The 61-member body, sponsored by the United Nations, lacks a formal negotiating agenda for 1997 due to disagreement between Western countries and non-aligned countries over how far to go toward nuclear disarmament, according to diplomats.

"By all means, strike bargains, seek trade-offs and manoeuvre in other ways to protect and advance your national, regional or group interests, but avoid 'hostage-taking' and stalemate," Downer told the Geneva forum.

"Focus on the arms control negotiations which are of most pressing concern to the international community...In 1997 I believe these to be: a treaty banning the production of fissile material for weapons purposes -- a 'cut-off' convention -- and a treaty which bans anti-personnel landmines totally," he said.

Australia, which has financed demining programmes in Angola, Afghanistan, Cambodia, Laos and Mozambique, will make a further contribution of A$4 million ($3 million) over the next three years for mine-clearance and rehabilitation work in Cambodia and Mozambique, according to Downer.
"Anti-personnel landmines are the great scourge of our day -- and sadly, will remain so for generations to come," he said.

"What is needed now is an instrument which will formalise the many national unilateral gestures into a legally-binding international regime which effectively outlaws anti-personnel landmines as a weapon of war and civilian terror," he added.
The Australian Foreign Minister, warning against a "partial solution" to the global landmines crisis through other channels, said that a landmines ban must be the product of the Conference.
Canada, which has pursued efforts to negotiate a ban through its "Ottawa process" of talks among 50 countries, has called for putting in place a landmine treaty by December 1997.
However, China and Russia -- among the top mine producers and exporters -- are not taking part in the Ottawa talks.
